missingCandidates.title: Boosting CO2-to-Aviation Fuel Fraction over an Inverse Structured KFeZr Tandem Catalyst
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract CO2 hydrogenation to aviation fuel-range hydrocarbons (C8–C16) offers a route to lowering net carbon emissions in the aviation sector, but achieving high selectivity to this fraction remains challenging. Herein, we report a synergistic strategy integrating an inverse-structured KFeZr catalyst with a CO-mediated “hydrogen pump” mechanism over HZSM-5. The inverse architecture, characterized by highly dispersed ZrO2 nanodomains anchored on Fe phases, induces strong metal interactions that stabilize an optimal phase composition (Fe5C2/Fe3O4 ≈ 1.2). This configuration not only provides physical passivation of over-active chain-growth sites but also yields enriched oxygen vacancies and an approximately 3.2-fold increase in interfacial site density compared to conventional counterparts. Upon coupling with HZSM-5, the tandem system delivers a 22% increase in selectivity for the aviation fuel-range fraction. Mechanistic studies identify CO as a “hydrogen pump” that regulates hydrogen transfer within the zeolite, thereby promoting dehydrocyclization and aromatization; introducing CO into the feed further raises this selectivity to 39.7%. This work provides critical insights into interfacial design and intermediate-mediated hydrogen regulation for high-performance liquid fuel synthesis.

missingCandidates.title: Heterogenization of Ru(bda) Molecular Catalyst with Redox-Active and Proton-Buffering Porphyrin Linkers for Acidic Water Oxidation
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract We report a porphyrin-bridged Ru(bda) coordination polymer integrated with carbon nanotubes, constructed from the well-defined homogeneous water oxidation catalyst in acid. The porphyrin linker simultaneously provides redox activity and proton-buffering functionality, enabling acidic water oxidation at an ultralow Ru loading (0.021 mgRu·cm–2). The resulting composite reaches current densities up to 200 mA·cm–2 in acid, exceeding previously reported molecular water oxidation catalyst-based anodes by one to two orders of magnitude. At identical metal loadings, it also outperforms both RuO2 and IrO2 benchmarks in both activity and stability. Electrochemical, spectroscopic, and theoretical results support porphyrin protonation and reversible oxidation, suggesting that ligand redox activity, together with proton management, contributes to the enhanced catalytic performance. These findings underscore the transformative potential of ligand engineering in molecular integration strategies for advancing artificial photosynthetic energy conversion systems.

missingCandidates.title: The Chameleon Role of Interfacial Hydroxyls: Reaction-Condition-Dependent Dynamics in Methanol Electro-Oxidation
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract The electrocatalytic oxidation of methanol on platinum represents a model system for alcohol fuel-cell chemistry, yet the precise role of interfacial hydroxyl (OH*), a key oxidative species, remains contentious and is often viewed simplistically as either a co-reactant or a poison. Herein, ab initio molecular dynamics simulations with explicit solvation were employed to transcend this binary perspective, revealing OH* as a dynamic interfacial mediator whose coverage influences methanol activation and mechanistic pathways. Under oxidative potentials, increasing OH* coverage leads to the formation of an interfacial adsorbate layer interconnected by hydrogen bonds. Frequent proton transfer within this layer facilitates spontaneous O–H bond cleavage of methanol, while fluctuations in the hydrogen-bond network further promote its pre-oxidation and activation. In contrast, OH*-mediated C–H oxidation involves a high free-energy barrier, and increasing OH* coverage reduces the availability of Pt sites required for C–H dissociation, potentially contributing to surface poisoning. Importantly, site competition induced by high OH* coverage also alters the configuration of the reaction-generated HCHO intermediate, reducing the accessibility of further C–H cleavage toward CO* while enabling direct reaction with OH* toward formate through a CO*-free pathway. Together, these results reveal a coverage-dependent trade-off among O–H activation, the availability of Pt sites for C–H bond cleavage, and subsequent pathway selection. Regulating interfacial OH* coverage therefore provides a possible means to tune methanol oxidation activity and pathway selectivity.

missingCandidates.title: Uncovering Functional Distant Mutations by Ultrahigh-Throughput Screening of Dehalogenases
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Conformational dynamics play a central role in enzyme function by controlling substrate access and productive binding. Yet, mutations that beneficially modulate these properties are difficult to identify. Here, we used ultrahigh-throughput fluorescence-activated droplet sorting (FADS) with a bulky fluorogenic substrate derived from coumarin (COU-3) to impose steric selection pressure on the haloalkane dehalogenase LinB. Screening a focused library yielded five single substitutions located 11.5–15.5 Å from the catalytic center. Variant I138N showed a fourfold increase in catalytic efficiency towards COU-3 through reduced KM and increased kcat, associated with increased cap-domain flexibility and facilitated substrate entry. In contrast, variant P208S markedly reduced substrate inhibition and shifted specificity towards bulkier iodinated haloalkanes by reshaping its tunnel environment. Integrated kinetic and structural analyses revealed that screening with bulky substrates directs selection towards distal regions controlling substrate access and unproductive binding. These findings demonstrate that combining ultrahigh-throughput FADS with focused library design can reveal dynamic mechanisms of enzyme adaptation that remain challenging to anticipate using conventional rational-design approaches.

missingCandidates.title: A Base Promoted Synthesis of Indazolo[2,3- a ]quinolines from Isatogens and 2-(2-Aminophenyl)acetonitriles
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract A transition-metal-free, base-promoted one-pot cascade cyclization strategy has been developed for the construction of indazolo[2,3-a]quinolines utilizing isatogens and 2-(2-aminophenyl)acetonitriles as precursors. This protocol enables the simultaneous formation of C–C, C–N, and N–N bonds to access complex tetracyclic frameworks. Preliminary photophysical characterization reveals significant fluorescence emission, indicating that the compound possesses promising optical properties for further investigations. The synthetic utility of this protocol is further underscored by its application in the Rh-catalyzed construction of highly-fused polycyclic cinnolinium salts.

Revival of Thermal Aziridine–Alkene Cycloaddition: Pyrrolidine Synthesis in Terpenoid-Based Deep Eutectic Solvents
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract A synthesis of pyrrolidines via atom-economic aziridine–alkene cycloaddition mediated by hydrophobic deep eutectic solvents (HDESs) is reported. HDESs, prepared from naturally occurring terpenoid compounds, serve as high-boiling reaction media and as alternatives to conventional petroleum-based solvents. This protocol proceeds in the presence of air without any special precautions, offering an approach to highly substituted pyrrolidine scaffolds. A broad range of N-aryl aziridines is used as azomethine ylide precursors, delivering pyrrolidines in up to 94% isolated yield. The methodology is further extended to a one-pot double cycloaddition directly from azide starting material, with solvent reusability and gram-scale synthesis also demonstrated.

Switchable quantum dot photoluminescence across a broad spectrum with all-visible-light activated diarylethene photoswitches
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Precise and reversible photoluminescence switching is highly attractive for optical memory, bioimaging, and smart displays. However, achieving broadband photoluminescence modulation through a simple and general strategy remains challenging, while the ultraviolet light requirement of most molecular photoswitches limits practical applications. Here, we achieve all-visible-light activated reversible photoluminescence modulation of quantum dots across an ultrawide spectral range of nearly 500 nm from blue to near-infrared region using diarylethene photoswitches. In the ring-open form of diarylethenes, quantum dots emitting blue, green, red, white and near-infrared light remain in the photoluminescence on-state. Under 405 nm irradiation, diarylethenes undergo ring-closure through triplet sensitization by CdS quantum dots, resulting in significant photoluminescence quenching to the off-state, with the maximum efficiency of 99.6% and an on/off ratio up to 250. Green-light irradiation reverses the diarylethenes back to the ring-open form, fully restoring the photoluminescence on-state. Our approach further enables reversible multi-level data storage and near-infrared anti-counterfeiting, highlighting the potential for smart light-responsive materials and optoelectronic devices.

Photocatalyst-Free Visible-Light-Mediated Synthesis of β-(Trifluoromethyl)alkenyl Ketoximes Using 2-Bromo-3,3,3-trifluoropropene as a Radical Precursor
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract We report a photocatalyst-free, visible-light-mediated difunctionalization of alkenes employing 2-bromo-3,3,3-trifluoropropene (BTP) as a radical precursor. This protocol operates under mild conditions using potassium formate as an electron transfer reagent and tert-butyl nitrite (TBN) as a hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) reagent, enabling efficient β-(trifluoromethyl)alkenyl ketoxime synthesis. Notably, no photocatalyst or transition metal is required, yet excellent stereoselectivity of the conjugated terminal alkene is achieved. Furthermore, this method exhibits a broad substrate scope and good functional group tolerance, accommodating diverse alkene classes.

missingCandidates.title: Computational Insights into Catalytic Hydrogenation over M6O8-Node MOFs: From Active-Site Engineering to Data-Driven Catalyst Design
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) containing M6O8 secondary building units (SBUs) have attracted considerable attention as hydrogenation catalysts because of their structural robustness, tunable coordination environments, and diverse opportunities for active-site engineering. In recent years, density functional theory (DFT) and related computational approaches have become indispensable tools for elucidating catalytic mechanisms and guiding catalyst design. This review summarizes recent theoretical advances in catalytic hydrogenation over M6O8-node MOFs, with particular emphasis on active-site engineering strategies, including metal doping, single-atom anchoring, metal cluster encapsulation, and ligand functionalization. Their effects on key catalytic processes, such as H2 activation, intermediate stabilization, and reaction energy barriers, are systematically discussed. We further highlight the electronic structure origins of catalytic performance, focusing on descriptors such as charge transfer, d-band center modulation, and frontier orbital interactions that govern activity and selectivity. In addition, emerging data-driven approaches are reviewed for their potential to establish structure–property relationships, enable high-throughput screening, and accelerate catalyst discovery. Current challenges in theoretical studies, including model idealization and the limited description of realistic reaction environments, are also discussed.

missingCandidates.title: Light-Accelerated Iridium-Catalyzed C–H Borylation
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Here, we report a mild, light-assisted iridium-catalyzed C–H borylation protocol for organic substrates. We demonstrate that adapting the Ishiyama–Tagaki–Miyaura–Hartwig (ITMH) protocol for C–H borylation to proceed under photochemical conditions imparts a pronounced rate enhancement compared to the established dark reaction. This photochemistry methodology achieves higher yields across a broad range of substrates and is easily scalable using continuous flow technology.
